reasoning: Plan A is the better training plan for a trail runner aiming to become faster because it incorporates more targeted intensity work, specifically tempo runs, which are crucial for building the sustainable strength needed for faster times on trails. Plan B focuses almost entirely on easy, consistent runs, which is good for building a base but doesn't adequately address the speed and lactate threshold development required for improvement. Plan A’s inclusion of two threshold sessions per week, alongside the longer runs, provides a more effective stimulus for increasing the runner’s ability to maintain a faster pace for longer distances. While Plan B has a slightly longer total running time, the quality of the workouts in Plan A is superior for the stated goal.
